claim: Breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs) contribute to intra-tumoral heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance.
source: Breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs) contribute to intra-tumoral heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that reflects established knowledge in the field about BCSCs.

claim: Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null mammary tumors each corresponded to a spectrum of minimally overlapping cell differentiation states without a universal BCSC population.
source: Through single-cell RNA-sequencing, we found that Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null mammary tumors each corresponded to a spectrum of minimally overlapping cell differentiation states without a universal BCSC population.
evidence: This claim is supported by the single-cell RNA-sequencing data presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figures 1-3.

claim: These tumors contained distinct lineage-specific tumor propagating cells (TPCs) reflective of the self-sustaining capabilities of lineage-specific stem/progenitor cells in the mammary epithelial hierarchy.
source: Instead, our analyses revealed that these tumors contained distinct lineage-specific tumor propagating cells (TPCs) and this is reflective of the self-sustaining capabilities of lineage-specific stem/progenitor cells in the mammary epithelial hierarchy.
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis of scRNA-seq data and is supported by inference from the observed patterns of cell states.

claim: CD14 is a TPC marker in the Neu tumor.
source: By understanding the respective tumor hierarchies, we were able to identify CD14 as a TPC marker in the Neu tumor.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data including scRNA-seq analysis, immunohistochemistry, and limiting dilution transplantation assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: Multiple breast cancer subtypes co-exist within tumors.
source: Additionally, single-cell breast cancer subtype stratification revealed the co-existence of multiple breast cancer subtypes within tumors.
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell intrinsic molecular subtype assignment data presented in Figure 6.

claim: The mammary gland is a bi-layered epithelial organ which consists of basal as well as myoepithelial cells in the outer layer.
source: The mammary gland is a bi-layered epithelial organ which consists of basal as well as myoepithelial cells in the outer layer.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammary gland structure.

claim: The inner epithelium comprises of luminal cells which can be broadly classified into the hormone-sensing lineage (estrogen receptor + or progesterone receptor +, ER+/PR+) and the secretory alveolar lineage.
source: The inner epithelium comprises of luminal cells which can be broadly classified into the hormone-sensing lineage (estrogen receptor + or progesterone receptor +, ER+/PR+) and the secretory alveolar lineage (Bach et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bach et al., 2017.

claim: During embryonic developmental stages, bipotent mammary stem cells (MaSCs) with hybrid basal-luminal gene expression patterns and the ability to give rise to both layers of the developed mammary epithelium have been described.
source: During embryonic developmental stages, bipotent mammary stem cells (MaSCs) with hybrid basal-luminal gene expression patterns and the ability to give rise to both layers of the developed mammary epithelium have been described (Pal et al., 2017; Spike et al., 2012; Wuidart et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pal et al., 2017; Spike et al., 2012; Wuidart et al., 2018.

claim: Postnatally, the hybrid basal-luminal gene signatures diminish and eventually leads to the bifurcation of unipotent basal and luminal lineage stem/progenitor cells respectively by the onset of puberty in mice.
source: Postnatally, the hybrid basal-luminal gene signatures diminish and eventually leads to the bifurcation of unipotent basal and luminal lineage stem/progenitor cells respectively by the onset of puberty in mice (Giraddi et al., 2018; Pal et al., 2017; Van Keymeulen et al., 2011; Wuidart et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Giraddi et al., 2018; Pal et al., 2017; Van Keymeulen et al., 2011; Wuidart et al., 2018.

claim: The ER+ and ER- luminal lineages can respectively self-sustain, through multiple cycles of pregnancy, lactation and involution.
source: Recent insights from lineage tracing in mouse experiments have also revealed that the ER+ and ER- luminal lineages can respectively self-sustain, through multiple cycles of pregnancy, lactation and involution (Van Keymeulen et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Van Keymeulen et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017.

claim: There is cumulative evidence to support the existence of primitive bipotent fetal-MaSCs (fMaSCs), quiescent adult-MaSCs (aMaSCs), basal-lineage SCs, ER- luminal SCs and ER+ luminal SCs at varying timepoints of mammary gland development in the mouse.
source: Altogether, there is cumulative evidence to support the existence of primitive bipotent fetal-MaSCs (fMaSCs) (Spike et al., 2012; Wuidart et al., 2018), quiescent adult-MaSCs (aMaSCs) (Fu et al., 2017; Rios et al., 2014), basal-lineage SCs (Shackleton et al., 2006; Van Keymeulen et al., 2011), ER- luminal SCs (Wang et al., 2017) and ER+ luminal SCs (Van Keymeulen et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017) at varying timepoints of mammary gland development in the mouse.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: There is a milieu of long-lived SCs/progenitors within the mouse mammary gland that could be candidates for transformation and potential tumor-initiating cells.
source: As such, there is a milieu of long-lived SCs/progenitors within the mouse mammary gland that could be candidates for transformation and potential tumor-initiating cells, but each with properties that are unique to a particular lineage or developmental timepoint.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cumulative evidence about mammary stem cells and progenitors.

claim: Neoplastic transformation of cells can lead to plasticity and the acquisition of stem/progenitor-like states.
source: Alternatively, neoplastic transformation of cells can also lead to plasticity (Koren et al., 2015; Molyneux et al., 2010) and the acquisition of any one of the aforementioned stem/progenitor-like states could have a unique role in tumor progression.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Koren et al., 2015; Molyneux et al., 2010.

claim: It has been proposed that differentiation hierarchies exist among tumor cells, with cancer stem cells (CSCs) residing at the apex of the hierarchy within tumors.
source: In the context of cancer, it has been proposed that differentiation hierarchies also exist among tumor cells, with cancer stem cells (CSCs) residing at the apex of the hierarchy within tumors (Nguyen et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nguyen et al., 2012.

claim: Major gaps remain in the conceptual framework of breast CSCs (BCSCs), particularly in light of recent insights from the normal mammary differentiation hierarchy.
source: Although much progress has been made since the initial prospective isolation of CSCs in breast tumors (Al-Hajj et al., 2003), major gaps remain in the conceptual framework of breast CSCs (BCSCs), particularly in light of recent insights from the normal mammary differentiation hierarchy (Fu et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2018; Van Keymeulen et al., 2017; Van Keymeulen et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2017; Wuidart et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an assessment based on the literature and supported by citations.

claim: Multiple distinct markers can enrich for BCSC populations such as CD44+/CD24-, ALDH+, HER2+, CD29hi and side population cells.
source: An additional confounding factor has been the description of multiple distinct markers that can enrich for BCSC populations such as CD44+/CD24- (Al-Hajj et al., 2003), ALDH+ (Ginestier et al., 2007), HER2+ (Ithimakin et al., 2013), CD29hi (Kouros-Mehr et al., 2008) and side population cells (Britton et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: The CD44+/CD24- and ALDH+ markers identify minimally overlapping populations with epithelial to mesenchymal (EMT)-like and mesenchymal to epithelial (MET)-like characteristics, respectively.
source: Recent studies have shown that the CD44+/CD24- and ALDH+ markers identify minimally overlapping populations and each of these sub-populations exhibit epithelial to mesenchymal (EMT)-like and mesenchymal to epithelial (MET)-like characteristics, respectively (Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Liu et al., 2014.

claim: Distinct BCSC populations have differential preferences for signaling and metabolic pathways.
source: Distinct BCSC populations have also been shown to have differential preferences for signaling and metabolic pathways (Luo et al., 2018; Roarty et al., 2017; Yeo et al., 2016), suggesting the need to account for these BCSC populations separately when it comes to therapeutic targeting.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Luo et al., 2018; Roarty et al., 2017; Yeo et al., 2016.

claim: Not all previously characterized BCSC markers have been investigated concurrently in an exhaustive manner.
source: It is also important to note that not all previously characterized BCSC markers have been investigated concurrently in an exhaustive manner (Hwang-Verslues et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hwang-Verslues et al., 2009.

claim: The mammary differentiation hierarchy has been pivotal in guiding the stratification of breast cancer subtypes.
source: The mammary differentiation hierarchy has also been pivotal in guiding the stratification of breast cancer subtypes (Visvader and Clevers, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Visvader and Clevers, 2016.

claim: Immunohistochemical analysis of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and HER2 receptor enables a crude association with the hormone-sensing lineage (ER+, PR+) and basal-like (ER-, PR-, HER2-) subtypes of breast cancer.
source: Immunohistochemical analysis of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and HER2 receptor enables a crude association with the hormone-sensing lineage (ER+, PR+) and basal-like (ER-, PR-, HER2-) subtypes of breast cancer.
evidence: This is established knowledge about breast cancer classification.

claim: Basal-like breast cancers are associated with mouse fMaSCs.
source: Parallels between the intrinsic molecular subtypes of breast cancer (Perou et al., 2000; Prat et al., 2010) and mammary differentiation states can also be observed with basal-like breast cancers being associated with mouse fMaSCs (Pal et al., 2017; Spike et al., 2012), claudin-low breast cancers with mouse aMaSCs (Fu et al., 2017) and luminal-A breast cancers with the hormone-sensing lineage.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pal et al., 2017; Spike et al., 2012.

claim: Claudin-low breast cancers are associated with mouse aMaSCs.
source: Parallels between the intrinsic molecular subtypes of breast cancer (Perou et al., 2000; Prat et al., 2010) and mammary differentiation states can also be observed with basal-like breast cancers being associated with mouse fMaSCs (Pal et al., 2017; Spike et al., 2012), claudin-low breast cancers with mouse aMaSCs (Fu et al., 2017) and luminal-A breast cancers with the hormone-sensing lineage.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Fu et al., 2017.

claim: Luminal-A breast cancers are associated with the hormone-sensing lineage.
source: Parallels between the intrinsic molecular subtypes of breast cancer (Perou et al., 2000; Prat et al., 2010) and mammary differentiation states can also be observed with basal-like breast cancers being associated with mouse fMaSCs (Pal et al., 2017; Spike et al., 2012), claudin-low breast cancers with mouse aMaSCs (Fu et al., 2017) and luminal-A breast cancers with the hormone-sensing lineage.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Perou et al., 2000; Prat et al., 2010.

claim: TPCs which occupy a less-differentiated cell state could correspond to a different breast cancer subtype relative to bulk tumor cells.
source: By extension, TPCs which occupy a less-differentiated cell state could correspond to a different breast cancer subtype relative to bulk tumor cells.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the relationship between cell states and subtypes.

claim: Breast cancer subtype heterogeneity within mouse models of breast cancer has not been well characterized.
source: An increasing number of observations support this notion (Chung et al., 2017; Roarty et al., 2017) but breast cancer subtype heterogeneity within mouse models of breast cancer has not been well characterized.
evidence: This is an assessment of the state of the field supported by citations.

claim: Tumor cells from different mouse models of breast cancer cluster separately with distinct signatures of mammary lineage markers.
source: Tumor cells from different mouse models of breast cancer cluster separately with distinct signatures of mammary lineage markers
evidence: This claim is supported by the scRNA-seq data and analysis presented in Figure 1.

claim: MMTV-Neu tumors were ER-/PR-/HER2+.
source: Essentially, the MMTV-Neu tumors examined were ER-/PR-/HER2+ while the MMTV-PyMT tumors were ER-/PR-/HER2lo (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: MMTV-PyMT tumors were ER-/PR-/HER2lo.
source: Essentially, the MMTV-Neu tumors examined were ER-/PR-/HER2+ while the MMTV-PyMT tumors were ER-/PR-/HER2lo (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: BRCA1-null tumors were ER-/PR-/HER-.
source: Complementarily, Brca1F/F Trp53F/F Krt14-Cre mice develop mammary tumors (Liu et al., 2007) (designated as BRCA1-null tumors) which mimic basal-like breast cancers and were ER-/PR-/HER- (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A total of 11842 cells were sequenced from all three tumor types.
source: A total of 11842 cells were sequenced from all three tumor types and after rigorous quality control filtering (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D), 9983 cells (4154, 3545 and 2284 cells for Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumors, respectively) were retained for subsequent analyses.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data collection.

claim: After quality control filtering, 9983 cells (4154, 3545 and 2284 cells for Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumors, respectively) were retained for subsequent analyses.
source: A total of 11842 cells were sequenced from all three tumor types and after rigorous quality control filtering (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D), 9983 cells (4154, 3545 and 2284 cells for Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumors, respectively) were retained for subsequent analyses.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data after quality control.

claim: On average, between 2205 to 3363 unique genes were detected for cells from each tumor sample.
source: On average, between 2205 to 3363 unique genes were detected for cells from each tumor sample (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Cells from both replicates were overlapping to a large degree despite sequencing the tumor replicates in a separate batch.
source: Despite sequencing the tumor replicates in a separate batch, initial analysis of cells through dimensionality reduction algorithms (Bioconductor: scran) revealed that cells from both replicates were overlapping to a large degree (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Replicates of respective tumor types had a high degree of concordance (Pearson correlation coefficients > 0.97 between respective replicates for all tumor types).
source: Moreover, replicates of respective tumor types were clustering together (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B) and had a high degree of concordance (Pearson correlation coefficients > 0.97 between respective replicates for all tumor types, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–E), indicating that batch effects were minimal.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–E.

claim: Batch effects were minimal.
source: Moreover, replicates of respective tumor types were clustering together (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B) and had a high degree of concordance (Pearson correlation coefficients > 0.97 between respective replicates for all tumor types, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–E), indicating that batch effects were minimal.
evidence: This is an inference based on the high concordance between replicates.

claim: Among these cells, the majority were more closely associated with a G1 cell cycle state and less than 2.5% of cells were either in G2/M or S phases.
source: Among these cells, the majority were more closely associated with a G1 cell cycle state and less than 2.5% of cells were either in G2/M or S phases (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell cycle analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–D.

claim: Normal mammary epithelial cell (MEC) contamination was inferred to be minimal among the cells examined (Cells without CNV in Neu: 0.4%, PyMT: 0%, BRCA1-null: 8.8%).
source: Additionally, normal mammary epithelial cell (MEC) contamination was inferred to be minimal among the cells examined (Cells without CNV in Neu: 0.4%, PyMT: 0%, BRCA1-null: 8.8%) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by CNV analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4E–F.

claim: Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumor cells formed three distinct groups with minimal overlap between cells of distinct tumor types.
source: Initial visualization of the data through t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) plots showed that Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumor cells formed three distinct groups (Figure 1B) with minimal overlap between cells of distinct tumor types, which is consistent with each of these models being driven by distinct oncogenic events.
evidence: This claim is supported by t-SNE analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The three main groups could be further subdivided into six clusters upon unsupervised clustering analysis.
source: These three main groups could be further subdivided into six clusters upon unsupervised clustering analysis by a shared nearest-neighbor clustering approach (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The basal-like BRCA1-null cells had increased expression of basal-associated genes such as Krt14, Vim and Sparc.
source: The basal-like BRCA1-null cells had increased expression of basal-associated genes such as Krt14, Vim and Sparc (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1D–E.

claim: BRCA1-null tumor cells could be segregated into cells with basal (Cluster 4) and mesenchymal (Cluster 5) features.
source: Intriguingly, the BRCA1-null tumor cells could be segregated further into cells with basal (Cluster 4) and mesenchymal (Cluster 5) features, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering and gene expression analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cluster 4 cells expressed higher levels of epithelial genes (Cldn4, Cldn3, Epcam) whereas Cluster 5 was defined by expression of mesenchymal genes (Vim, Sparc, Col3a1, Bgn).
source: Cluster 4 cells expressed higher levels of epithelial genes (Cldn4, Cldn3, Epcam) whereas Cluster 5 was defined by expression of mesenchymal genes (Vim, Sparc, Col3a1, Bgn) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: PyMT tumor cells had higher levels of Ltf, Spp1, Anxa1 and Cldn4 distinguishing them from Neu and BRCA1-null tumor cells.
source: In the case of PyMT tumor cells, higher levels of Ltf, Spp1, Anxa1 and Cldn4 distinguish them from Neu and BRCA1-null tumor cells (Figure 1D and F), and some of these genes have been associated with luminal progenitors (Nguyen et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1D and F.

claim: Levels of the luminal progenitor marker Aldh1a3 was exclusively detected in PyMT tumor cells.
source: In addition, levels of the luminal progenitor marker Aldh1a3 was exclusively detected in PyMT tumor cells (Figure 1F), indicating that these tumors consist of cells associated with a primitive luminal cell state (Eirew et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Neu tumor cells can be divided into Cluster 1 and Cluster 2, both expressing higher levels of genes associated with secretory alveolar differentiation such as Csn1s1, Lalba and Tspan8.
source: Neu tumor cells can be divided into Cluster 1 and Cluster 2, both expressing higher levels of genes associated with secretory alveolar differentiation such as Csn1s1, Lalba and Tspan8 (Figure 1D and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1D and G.

claim: Levels of some alveolar differentiation genes such as Cited4 and Tspan8 were marginally higher in Cluster 1, indicating that Cluster 1 cells were more differentiated along the alveolar lineage relative to Cluster 2.
source: Levels of some alveolar differentiation genes such as Cited4 and Tspan8 were marginally higher in Cluster 1, indicating that Cluster 1 cells were more differentiated along the alveolar lineage relative to Cluster 2 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression data shown in Figure 1D and inference about differentiation state.

claim: Mammary tumors driven by different oncogenic events contained clusters of tumor cells that were associated with distinct developmental cell states with minimal overlap between the tumor types.
source: Altogether, these results revealed that mammary tumors driven by different oncogenic events contained clusters of tumor cells that were associated with distinct developmental cell states with minimal overlap between the tumor types.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumor cell clusters overlapped with distinct normal MEC clusters through integration analysis.
source: We found that Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumor cell clusters overlapped with distinct normal MEC clusters through this analysis (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the integrated analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: BRCA1-null tumor cells were distributed amongst distinct clusters associated with C13, basal cells during gestation (C13:Bsl-G) and C12, basal cells (C12:Bsl).
source: BRCA1-null tumor cells were distributed amongst distinct clusters associated with C13, basal cells during gestation (C13:Bsl-G) and C12, basal cells (C12:Bsl) (Figure 2C), consistent with our initial observations of these cells having increased expression of basal genes (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the integrated analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: BRCA1-null cells also clustered amongst C10, alveolar progenitors during gestation (C10:AvP-G), C15, PROCR+ cells that arise during lactation (C15: Prc) and C18, fibroblasts with mesenchymal features (C18:Fibroblasts).
source: In addition, BRCA1-null cells also clustered amongst C10, alveolar progenitors during gestation (C10:AvP-G), C15, PROCR+ cells that arise during lactation (C15: Prc) and C18, fibroblasts with mesenchymal features (C18:Fibroblasts) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the integrated analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A spectrum of BRCA1-null tumor cells can be found distributed between clusters C12:Bsl and C10:AvP-G, representing a population with hybrid basal-alveolar gene expression.
source: It is also worth noting that a spectrum of BRCA1-null tumor cells can be found distributed between clusters C12:Bsl and C10:AvP-G (Figure 2C). These cells could represent a population with hybrid basal-alveolar gene expression, which have also been documented by Bach et al. and were designated as C20 (Bach et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is based on the distribution of cells in Figure 2C and inference about their identity.

claim: PyMT tumor cells primarily clustered between C6, luminal progenitors from nulliparous glands (C6:LP-NP) and C7, luminal progenitors during involution (C7:LP-PI).
source: As for PyMT tumor cells (Figure 2F), they primarily clustered between C6, luminal progenitors from nulliparous glands (C6:LP-NP) and C7, luminal progenitors during involution (C7:LP-PI), consistent with their association with a luminal progenitor gene expression signature seen in our initial analysis (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the integrated analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: A small proportion of PyMT cells were converging with C10, alveolar progenitors during gestation (C10:AvP-G), indicating the priming of these luminal progenitor-like cells towards the alveolar lineage.
source: A small proportion of PyMT cells were also converging with C10, alveolar progenitors during gestation (C10:AvP-G), indicating the priming of these luminal progenitor-like cells towards the alveolar lineage (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is based on the distribution of cells in Figure 2F and inference about their differentiation state.

claim: PyMT tumor cells that were proximal to the C6:LP-NP cluster exhibited elevated Aldh1a3 expression.
source: Interestingly, PyMT tumor cells that were proximal to the C6:LP-NP cluster exhibited elevated Aldh1a3 expression (Figure 2G), whereas there was an enrichment of cells with high Mfge8 expression towards the C7:LP-PI cluster (Figure 2H), suggesting that the post-involution state is associated with increased Mfge8 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: There was an enrichment of cells with high Mfge8 expression towards the C7:LP-PI cluster, suggesting that the post-involution state is associated with increased Mfge8 expression.
source: Interestingly, PyMT tumor cells that were proximal to the C6:LP-NP cluster exhibited elevated Aldh1a3 expression (Figure 2G), whereas there was an enrichment of cells with high Mfge8 expression towards the C7:LP-PI cluster (Figure 2H), suggesting that the post-involution state is associated with increased Mfge8 expression.
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression data shown in Figure 2H and inference about the post-involution state.

claim: Neu tumor cells were mostly clustered between C9, alveolar differentiated cells during lactation (C9: AvD-L) and C11, alveolar progenitor cells of lactating glands (C11:AvP-L).
source: Comparison of Neu tumor cells with the various clusters in Bach et al.'s dataset showed that they were mostly clustered between C9, alveolar differentiated cells during lactation (C9: AvD-L) and C11, alveolar progenitor cells of lactating glands (C11:AvP-L)(Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by the integrated analysis shown in Figure 2I.

claim: A portion of Neu tumor cells adjacent to C11 extend into and overlap with C7, luminal progenitor cells from post-involution (C7:LP-PI).
source: A portion of tumor cells adjacent to C11 also extend into and overlap with C7, luminal progenitor cells from post-involution (C7:LP-PI).
evidence: This is an observation from the integrated analysis.

claim: Neu tumor cells were scattered between C8, alveolar differentiated cells during gestation (C8:AvD-G) and C10, alveolar progenitor cells during gestation (C10:AvP-G).
source: We also noted Neu tumor cells scattered between C8, alveolar differentiated cells during gestation (C8:AvD-G) and C10, alveolar progenitor cells during gestation (C10:AvP-G).
evidence: This is an observation from the integrated analysis.

claim: Neu tumors contained cells which corresponded to a spectrum of differentiation states within the secretory alveolar lineage (i.e. C7:LP-PI → C11 and C10: AvP → C9 and C8: AvD).
source: These results were consistent with the initial analyses for Neu tumor cells that exhibited a secretory alveolar gene expression signature (Figure 1G), and also suggested these Neu tumors contained cells which corresponded to a spectrum of differentiation states within the secretory alveolar lineage (i.e. C7:LP-PI → C11 and C10: AvP → C9 and C8: AvD).
evidence: This is an inference based on the distribution of Neu tumor cells across different normal cell clusters.

claim: The increasing level of differentiation in the cascade among the population of Neu tumor cells was supported by the gradual change in expression of the milk protein gene Csn1s2a.
source: The increasing level of differentiation in this cascade among the population of Neu tumor cells was also supported by the gradual change in expression of the milk protein gene Csn1s2a in the main cluster of Neu tumor cells (Figure 2J).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The distinct pattern of Col9a1 expression among Neu tumor cells suggested the clustering of alveolar cells from gestation and lactation timepoints respectively.
source: Additionally, the distinct pattern of Col9a1 expression among Neu tumor cells (Figure 2K) suggested the clustering of alveolar cells from gestation and lactation timepoints respectively.
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression data shown in Figure 2K and inference about cell clustering.

claim: The analysis utilizing Seurat v3 was robust and stable, as evidenced by the same pattern of overlap between tumor and normal cells from two other independent iterations.
source: Overall, this analysis utilizing Seurat v3 (Figure 2) was robust and stable, as evidenced by the same pattern of overlap between tumor and normal cells from two other independent iterations, utilizing independent sampling of random cells from Bach et al.'s dataset (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the reproducibility shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The majority of BRCA1-null cells were assigned into clusters 5 and 8 (41.5% and 20.6% of total BRCA1-null cells respectively), which contained C12:Bsl, C13:Bsl-G and C20 cells.
source: The majority of BRCA1-null cells were assigned into clusters 5 and 8 (41.5% and 20.6% of total BRCA1-null cells respectively), which contained C12:Bsl, C13:Bsl-G and C20 cells.
evidence: This claim is based on the clustering analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: 93% of PyMT tumor cells were assigned into cluster 0, which corresponded to the luminal progenitor populations C6:LP and C7:LP-PI.
source: In the case of PyMT tumor cells, 93% of cells were assigned into cluster 0, which corresponded to the luminal progenitor populations C6:LP and C7:LP-PI (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is based on the clustering analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Neu cells were assigned into Clusters 3 and 4 (33% and 7.7% of total Neu cells respectively), affirming the alveolar lineage association of these tumor cells.
source: Neu cells were also assigned into Clusters 3 and 4 (33% and 7.7% of total Neu cells respectively), further affirming the alveolar lineage association of these tumor cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is based on the clustering analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The bulk of Neu tumor cells (58%) were assigned into cluster 2, corresponding to C8:AvD-G cells.
source: The bulk of Neu tumor cells (58%) were assigned into cluster 2, corresponding to C8:AvD-G cells.
evidence: This claim is based on the clustering analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The association between tumor and normal cells through clustering corroborated the observations from t-SNE plots.
source: Overall, the association between tumor and normal cells through clustering (Figure 3) corroborated the observations from t-SNE plots (Figure 2), alleviating complications that may arise when interpreting distances in low dimensional space (Figure 2, t-SNE).
evidence: This is an assessment of the consistency between different analytical approaches.

claim: BRCA1-null tumor cells exhibited the lowest DPT, PyMT tumor cells had moderate DPT, whereas Neu tumor cells were associated with the highest DPT.
source: Accordingly, BRCA1-null tumor cells exhibited the lowest DPT, PyMT tumor cells had moderate DPT, whereas Neu tumor cells were associated with the highest DPT (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E.

claim: Only a small proportion of tumor cells from distinct tumor types overlapped at the intersection of branches in the cell state trajectory.
source: Evidently, a main root and two branches can be observed, but only a small proportion of tumor cells from distinct tumor types overlapped at the intersection of these branches (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by trajectory analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–C.

claim: Different tumor models comprised of cells which corresponded mostly to distinct spectrums of cell states.
source: Together, these results further substantiated the fact that these different tumor models comprised of cells which corresponded mostly to distinct spectrums of cell states.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the trajectory analysis.

claim: The BRCA1-null tumors can be clustered into five main clusters, designated as BRCA1-1 to BRCA1-5.
source: The BRCA1-null tumors can be clustered into five main clusters, designated as BRCA1-1 to BRCA1-5 (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 4A–B.

claim: The BRCA1-1 cluster consisted of proliferating cells with increased expression of cell cycle related genes such as Birc5, Tyms and Mki67.
source: The BRCA1-1 cluster consisted of proliferating cells with increased expression of cell cycle related genes such as Birc5, Tyms and Mki67.
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: BRCA1-5 was a cluster with strongest expression of prototypical basal genes such as Krt14 and Igfbp5.
source: BRCA1-5 was a cluster with strongest expression of prototypical basal genes such as Krt14 and Igfbp5.
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: BRCA1-2 cells exhibited a partial EMT gene expression pattern with moderate levels of collagens and the highest levels of EMT transcription factors such as Yap1, Twist1 and Zeb1.
source: Interestingly, BRCA1-2 cells exhibited a partial EMT gene expression pattern with moderate levels of collagens and the highest levels of EMT transcription factors such as Yap1, Twist1 and Zeb1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: BRCA1-3 cells expressed the highest levels of genes associated with fibroblasts.
source: On the other hand, BRCA1-3 cells expressed the highest levels of genes associated with fibroblasts (Figure 4B) and this would fit with our previous observations of a sub-population of BRCA1 null cells with mesenchymal characteristics (Figures 1–3).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Within BRCA1-null tumors, cells with features of AvPs (BRCA1-4) were present with elevated levels of Cldn3, Malat1, Krt18, Wfdc18 and Mfge8.
source: Within this predominantly basal tumor type, cells with features of AvPs (BRCA1-4) were also present with elevated levels of Cldn3, Malat1, Krt18, Wfdc18 and Mfge8.
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: PyMT cells were identified into three clusters, PyMT-1 to PyMT-3, which corresponded to LP-Involution (LP-PI) cells, Av-primed LPs and LPs respectively.
source: For PyMT cells, we identified three clusters, PyMT-1 to PyMT-3, which corresponded to LP-Involution (LP-PI) cells, Av-primed LPs and LPs respectively (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 4C–D.

claim: The involution genes elevated in PyMT-1 included Mfge8, Csf3, Spp1 and Ltf.
source: The involution genes elevated in PyMT-1 included Mfge8, Csf3, Spp1 and Ltf (Figure 4D, Figure 4—source data 3) which corresponded well to enrichment of gene ontologies (GO) such as 'lipopolysaccharide-mediated signaling' and 'positive regulation of phagocytosis' (Figure 4—source data 4).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression and GO analysis.

claim: PyMT-2 cells expressed higher levels of alveolar differentiation genes (Lalba, Wap, Csn1s1) and genes categorized under the GO 'oxidative phosphorylation'.
source: Apart from expressing higher levels of alveolar differentiation genes (Lalba, Wap, Csn1s1), PyMT-2 cells were also found to express higher levels of genes categorized under the GO, 'oxidative phosphorylation' (Figure 4—source data 4).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression and GO analysis.

claim: Upregulated genes for PyMT-3 cells were enriched for those categorized under 'glycolytic process', highlighting the possibility of metabolic heterogeneity between PyMT tumor populations.
source: Contrastingly, upregulated genes for PyMT-3 cells were enriched for those categorized under 'glycolytic process' (Figure 4—source data 4), highlighting the possibility of metabolic heterogeneity between these PyMT tumor populations.
evidence: This claim is based on GO analysis and inference about metabolic heterogeneity.

claim: 4T1 tumor analysis revealed the presence of three clusters designated as 4T1-1 to 4T1-3.
source: Nonetheless, intra-tumoral analysis revealed the presence of three clusters designated as 4T1-1 to 4T1-3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Cluster 4T1-1 showed increased co-expression of IFN signaling genes (Irf1, Irf8, Cxcl9, Cxcl10) and the proliferation marker gene Mki67.
source: Cluster 4T1-1 showed increased co-expression of IFN signaling genes (Irf1, Irf8, Cxcl9, Cxcl10) and the proliferation marker gene Mki67 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Immunohistochemical staining for IRF1 and Ki67 in serial sections of 4T1 tumors validated the presence of IRF1+ and Ki67+ cells within the same region of these tumors.
source: Immunohistochemical staining for IRF1 and Ki67 in serial sections of 4T1 tumors validated the presence of IRF1+ and Ki67+ cells within the same region of these tumors (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C), suggesting that activation of interferon signaling could be a driver for tumor growth in this model.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Cluster 4T1-3 had increased expression of MHC-II molecules such as H2-Ab1 and H2-Aa.
source: Another noteworthy feature of cells within this model was the increased expression of MHC-II molecules such as H2-Ab1 and H2-Aa in cluster 4T1-3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, Figure 4—source data 5).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Neu tumor cells revealed four clusters (Neu-1 to Neu-4) with well-defined characteristics to allow illustration of their hierarchical relationships.
source: Examination of Neu tumor cells revealed four clusters (Neu-1 to Neu-4) with well-defined characteristics to allow illustration of their hierarchical relationships (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: Neu-3 cells had increased expression of milk production related genes such as Lalba and can be defined by higher expression of Cited4, Cd36 and Aqp5 which corresponded to the AvD cell state.
source: Neu-3 cells had increased expression of milk production related genes such as Lalba and can be defined by higher expression of Cited4, Cd36 and Aqp5 which corresponded to the AvD cell state Figure 4F, Figure 4—source datas 6–7).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Neu-2 cluster had elevated expression of Cd14, Tnfrsf12a, Nfkbia, Bcl3 and Osmr.
source: Although cells within the Neu-2 cluster also exhibited increased milk production related genes, this population had elevated expression of Cd14, Tnfrsf12a, Nfkbia, Bcl3 and Osmr.
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The increased expression of Cd14 in the Neu-2 cluster led to the inference that these were AvP cells, since Cd14 has been described as a marker for progenitor cells.
source: The increased expression of Cd14 in this Neu-2 cluster led us to the inference that these were AvP cells, since Cd14 has been described as a marker for progenitor cells (Bach et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression and citation to Bach et al., 2017.

claim: Neu-1 cells expressed Cd14 along with increased LP-associated genes such as Cldn10, Malat1, and Krt18.
source: Neu-1 cells did express Cd14 along with increased LP-associated genes such as Cldn10, Malat1, and Krt18.
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis.

claim: Neu-1 cluster had lower expression of milk production genes, indicating that these cells were most closely associated with C7:LP-PI cells.
source: Moreover, this cluster had lower expression of milk production genes, which indicated that these cells were most closely associated with C7:LP-PI cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression patterns.

claim: Neu-4 was a smaller cluster of proliferating cells characterized by elevated Birc5, Tyms and Pcna.
source: Neu-4 was a smaller cluster of proliferating cells characterized by elevated Birc5, Tyms and Pcna.
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The presence of Neu-4 cells in opposing ends of t-SNE dimension one suggested that there were distinct cell states with proliferative potential in the Neu tumor model.
source: The presence of Neu-4 cells in opposing ends of t-SNE dimension one suggested that there were distinct cell states with proliferative potential in this tumor model (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the distribution of cells in t-SNE space shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Both Neu-1 and Neu-2 clusters expressed higher levels of the luminal progenitor marker, Cd14, along with other STAT3 target genes (Bcl3, Osmr) and Nfkbia.
source: Both Neu-1 and Neu-2 clusters expressed higher levels of the luminal progenitor marker, Cd14 (Asselin-Labat et al., 2011), along with other STAT3 target genes (Bcl3, Osmr [Clarkson et al., 2004]) and Nfkbia (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5A and supported by citations.

claim: The STAT3 pathway has been associated with acquisition of BCSC properties.
source: It is worth noting that the STAT3 pathway has been associated with acquisition of BCSC properties (Wei et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wei et al., 2014.

claim: CD14+ cells can be detected in a sub-population of Neu tumor cells by immuno-histochemistry.
source: We can also detect the presence of CD14+ cells in a sub-population of Neu tumor cells by immuno-histochemistry, validating the scRNA-seq observations (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Levels of Cd14, Bcl3, Osmr and Nfkbia were significantly increased in the CD14hi populations.
source: Consistently, levels of Cd14, Bcl3, Osmr and Nfkbia were significantly increased in the CD14hi populations (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The increased expression of STAT3 target genes in the CD14hi population was accompanied by elevated phospho-Stat3 levels.
source: The increased expression of STAT3 target genes in the CD14hi population was also accompanied by elevated phospho-Stat3 levels (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The CD14hi population exhibited increased tumorigenic potential with an estimated TPC frequency of 1/278 compared to 1/2295 for CD14lo/- cells (Chi-squared test, p=0.00134).
source: When transplanted into syngeneic FvB mice at limiting dilutions, the CD14hi population also exhibited increased tumorigenic potential with an estimated TPC frequency of 1/278 compared to 1/2295 for CD14lo/- cells (Chi-squared test, p=0.00134) (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by limiting dilution transplantation data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: CD14hi cells in the Neu tumors could be highly enriched for parity induced-MECs, that have been previously described to be BCSCs in this model.
source: These CD14hi cells in the Neu tumors could be highly enriched for parity induced-MECs, that have been previously described to be BCSCs in this model (Asselin-Labat et al., 2011; Henry et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a speculative inference supported by citations to Asselin-Labat et al., 2011; Henry et al., 2004.

claim: The Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumors each comprised of cells which corresponded to several intrinsic breast cancer subtypes.
source: Interestingly, the Neu, PyMT and BRCA1-null tumors each comprised of cells which corresponded to several intrinsic breast cancer subtypes (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell intrinsic molecular subtype assignment shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The BRCA1-null tumors had larger proportions of claudin-low and basal-like tumor cells.
source: The BRCA1-null tumors had larger proportions of claudin-low and basal-like tumor cells (Figure 6A), whereas Neu and PyMT tumors contained more luminal A and normal-like subtype cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell intrinsic molecular subtype assignment shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Neu and PyMT tumors contained more luminal A and normal-like subtype cells.
source: The BRCA1-null tumors had larger proportions of claudin-low and basal-like tumor cells (Figure 6A), whereas Neu and PyMT tumors contained more luminal A and normal-like subtype cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell intrinsic molecular subtype assignment shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The presence of mesenchymal populations in BRCA1-null tumors was concordant with the assignment of claudin-low subtypes in this tumor type.
source: The presence of mesenchymal populations in BRCA1-null tumors (Figures 3D and 4A) was also concordant with the assignment of claudin-low subtypes in this tumor type (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the concordance between mesenchymal features and claudin-low subtype.

claim: The observation of multiple breast cancer subtypes within a tumor warrants further investigation into its potential clinical significance.
source: Altogether, the observation of multiple breast cancer subtypes within a tumor warrants further investigation into its potential clinical significance.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.

claim: Each of the tumors investigated were likely to contain lineage specific TPCs respectively.
source: However, the results presented here do not exclude the possibility of the existence of universal BCSCs, because they may exist at frequencies that were not detectable based on the cell numbers examined (<0.5%). The sorting of CD24+ cells may also exclude cells that have undergone EMT but we utilized a less stringent CD24+ gating strategy (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) that still enabled the identification of mesenchymal populations, especially in the BRCA1-null tumors. Despite these potential limitations, our observations indicated that each of the tumors investigated were likely to contain lineage specific TPCs respectively.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data presented, acknowledging potential limitations.

claim: Patients expressing higher levels of the genes differentially expressed by clusters BRCA1-1 (Proliferating) and BRCA1-4 (Alveolar Progenitor-like) were associated with poorer relapse-free survival.
source: Interestingly, this analysis revealed that patients expressing higher levels of the genes differentially expressed by clusters BRCA1-1 (Proliferating) and BRCA1-4 (Alveolar Progenitor-like) respectively (Figure 4B), were associated with poorer relapse-free survival (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Cells from cluster BRCA1-3 were classified as tumor because they were predicted to harbor chromosomal amplification or deletion events.
source: Cells from cluster BRCA1-3 were classified as tumor because they were predicted to harbor chromosomal amplification or deletion events (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is based on CNV analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: CD14 protein expression can be detected in a subset of BRCA1-null mouse tumor cells.
source: Since CD14 protein expression can be detected in a subset of BRCA1-null mouse tumor cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), as well as human breast cancers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), further work will be necessary to validate its potential significance in human breast cancer.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CD14 protein expression can be detected in human breast cancers.
source: Since CD14 protein expression can be detected in a subset of BRCA1-null mouse tumor cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), as well as human breast cancers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), further work will be necessary to validate its potential significance in human breast cancer.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The proposed model incorporates the elaborate intricacy of the mammary differentiation hierarchy, which is a conceptual leap from the focus on just universal BCSCs that reside at the apex of the tumor hierarchy.
source: Importantly, our proposed model incorporates the elaborate intricacy of the mammary differentiation hierarchy, which is a conceptual leap from the focus on just universal BCSCs that reside at the apex of the tumor hierarchy.
evidence: This is a statement about the conceptual framework of the study.

claim: Progenitor-like cells and other intermediary states within the tumor hierarchy could be relevant.
source: As in the case of the Neu tumor (Figure 5), progenitor-like cells and other intermediary states within the tumor hierarchy could also be relevant.
evidence: This is an inference based on the findings in the Neu tumor.

claim: The more differentiated cell states may have a role in supporting tumor growth through a paracrine manner.
source: Even the more differentiated cell states may have a role in supporting tumor growth through a paracrine manner and similar mechanisms of cooperativity between tumor sub-populations have been documented (Cleary et al., 2014; Marusyk et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations to Cleary et al., 2014; Marusyk et al., 2014.

claim: The composition (hierarchical heterogeneity) of breast tumors may need to be accounted for to determine the combination of therapeutic agents that can effectively eliminate all the tumor sub-populations with discrete susceptibilities.
source: The composition (hierarchical heterogeneity) of breast tumors may need to be accounted for to determine the combination of therapeutic agents that can effectively eliminate all the tumor sub-populations with discrete susceptibilities (Yeo and Guan, 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about therapeutic implications supported by citation to Yeo and Guan, 2017.

claim: Single-cell intrinsic molecular subtyping could potentially play a role in illuminating the spectrum of hierarchical heterogeneity within tumors.
source: With regard to that, intrinsic molecular subtyping of breast cancers can be associated with particular tumor differentiation cell states (Visvader and Clevers, 2016) and single-cell intrinsic molecular subtyping (Chung et al., 2017; Yeo and Guan, 2017) could potentially play a role in illuminating the spectrum of hierarchical heterogeneity within tumors.
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations.

claim: Stratification strategies for single-cell classification will require further refinement because of the influence from cell-cycle-related genes.
source: Even then, stratification strategies for single-cell classification will require further refinement because of the influence from cell-cycle-related genes.
evidence: This is an assessment of the limitations of current methods.

claim: Diagnosing the intra-tumoral breast cancer subtype heterogeneity may provide an indication of the hierarchical heterogeneity within tumors and guide the selection of combinatorial therapeutic regimens.
source: Altogether, diagnosing the intra-tumoral breast cancer subtype heterogeneity may provide an indication of the hierarchical heterogeneity within tumors and guide the selection of combinatorial therapeutic regimens.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential clinical applications.

claim: The single-cell data can serve as an important reference point for future studies which perturb the dynamics of the sub-populations.
source: Although we have only analyzed these tumors under 'steady state' conditions, the single-cell data can serve as an important reference point for future studies which perturb the dynamics of the sub-populations.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential utility of the data for future research.

claim: The results unraveled the distinct spectrum of differentiation states within mammary tumors and indicate that these tumors contain lineage-specific stem/progenitor-like TPCs.
source: Crucially, our results unraveled the distinct spectrum of differentiation states within mammary tumors and indicate that these tumors contain lineage-specific stem/progenitor-like TPCs.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claim: The findings emphasize the need to account for the distinct spectrum of differentiation states within breast tumors to prevent therapeutic resistance.
source: This emphasizes the need to account for the distinct spectrum of differentiation states within breast tumors to prevent therapeutic resistance.
evidence: This is a statement about the implications of the findings for therapeutic strategies.
